entities.description: Black-owned funeral home founded 1933 by Rev. Andrew 'A.R.' Leak; still operating (flagship 7838 S. Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago); handled funerals for Sam Cooke (1964) and Rev. Jesse L. Jackson Sr. (2026).
entities.name: Leak & Sons Funeral Homes

entities.description: Founder of Leak & Sons Funeral Homes (1933); opened with savings from World's Fair work and a loan from his wife Dottie, per family accounts.
entities.name: Rev. Andrew "A.R." Leak

entities.description: Third-generation funeral director; mortuary science degree, Southern Illinois University (1989); public face of Leak & Sons' community role; died May 2026.
entities.name: Spencer Leak Jr.

entities.description: Wife of Rev. A.R. Leak; her loan ($500, per family account) capitalized the founding of Leak & Sons.
entities.name: Dottie Leak

entities.description: Black-owned funeral home at 4141 S. Cottage Grove (1947); received, opened, and prepared Emmett Till's body for public viewing, Sept 1955.
entities.name: A.A. Rayner & Sons Funeral Home

entities.description: Founder of A.A. Rayner & Sons (1947); mortuary training (Worsham, Prairie View A&M); livery manager at Metropolitan Funeral Home before founding.
entities.name: Ahmed A. Rayner Sr.

entities.description: Black-owned funeral home founded 1947 (purchased Bell Auto & Undertaking Co.); moved to 3232 S. King Dr 1969; Heritage Memorial Wall 1990; closed Dec 31, 2007.
entities.name: Griffin Funeral Home

entities.description: Funeral director; Worsham College 1934; civic leader (Lakeside Bank board 20+ yrs, Heritage Memorial Wall); Congressional Record tribute Dec 18, 1995.
entities.name: Ernest A. Griffin

entities.description: Licensed funeral director and embalmer; worked in Griffin family business from 1958; ran it after her husband's 1995 death until closure.
entities.name: Alyce Louise Carter Griffin

entities.description: Black-owned and managed cemetery founded 1927 in Alsip, Illinois; burial site of Emmett Till (Sept 6, 1955); 2025 National Register recommendation.
entities.name: Burr Oak Cemetery

entities.description: Church of God in Christ at 4021 S. State St, Chicago; site of Emmett Till's open-casket visitation and funeral (Sept 3, 1955); part of Emmett Till and Mamie Till-Mobley National Monument since July 25, 2023.
entities.name: Roberts Temple Church of God in Christ

entities.description: Mother of Emmett Till; insisted on open-casket funeral ('Let the people see what they did to my boy'); her decision is the political center of the Till sequence.
entities.name: Mamie Till-Mobley

entities.description: Mortuary college founded March 17, 1911 by Albert Worsham; trained A.A. Rayner Sr. and Ernest A. Griffin. Not Black-owned — a white-founded professional school Black Chicagoans used.
entities.name: Worsham College of Mortuary Science
sources: Illinois Board of Higher Education records

entities.description: Black funeral-directors' professional association; ~2,000 member firms; founding lineage disputed (1924 INFD Association → renamed 1957 vs. 'National Association of Negro Funeral Directors' per LOC).
entities.name: National Funeral Directors and Morticians Association
entities.verification_note: Founding lineage disputed; see red team.

entities.description: Black funeral home at 4445 S. King Dr; A.A. Rayner Sr. was livery manager here; building became Chicago Defender headquarters in May 2009.
entities.name: Metropolitan Funeral Home

entities.description: Black-owned insurance company; funeral-home affiliate employed A.A. Rayner Sr. as livery manager — the insurance-funeral nexus of Black Chicago's death-care economy.
entities.name: Chicago Metropolitan Mutual Life Assurance Co.

entities.description: Jackson, Mississippi undertaker; archivally documented use of funeral-home resources (vehicles, meeting space, funds, information) for Freedom Riders and civil-rights organizing (1961). National comparison case.
entities.name: Clarie Collins Harvey
sources: Sanders (2014), Journal of Mississippi History; Clarie Collins Harvey Papers, Amistad Research Center

entities.description: Philadelphia, 1787; founded by Richard Allen and Absalom Jones; pooled dues for funerals, sickness aid, and widow/child support — origin of the mutual-aid lineage behind Black funeral homes.
entities.name: Free African Society

entities.description: Birmingham, Alabama funeral home; documented community functions (youth baseball sponsorship, rides, meeting space, music lessons on the chapel piano) — national comparison.
entities.name: Poole Funeral Chapels

entities.description: Charlottesville, Virginia funeral home (oldest family-run in central Virginia); founder J.F. Bell trained as funeral director in Chicago; funeral-home vehicles seeded the city's first integrated taxi company — national comparison.
entities.name: J.F. Bell Funeral Home

entities.description: A.A. Rayner & Sons (1947–1955 location); received Emmett Till's body Sept 2, 1955.
entities.name: 4141 S. Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago

entities.description: Leak & Sons Funeral Homes flagship.
entities.name: 7838 S. Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago

entities.description: Griffin Funeral Home (1969–2007); Heritage Memorial Wall site.
entities.name: 3232 S. King Dr, Chicago

entities.description: Roberts Temple Church of God in Christ; Till funeral site; National Monument.
entities.name: 4021 S. State St, Chicago

entities.description: Burr Oak Cemetery; 150 acres; Till's burial site.
entities.name: 4400 W. 127th St, Alsip, IL

entities.description: Former Metropolitan Funeral Home; Chicago Defender HQ from May 2009.
entities.name: 4445 S. King Dr, Chicago

entities.description: Johnson Publishing Company offices (1949–1971) in a former funeral home.
entities.name: 1820 S. Michigan Ave, Chicago
